findings.finding: Owner rulings 329 A and 332 A open a DECODING-POLICY control axis at the Solver node. The R2b forced-close analysis found that the Solver's reasoning does not terminate on about 40 % of rows regardless of the budget (66 % of rows forced at 3,072 are still forced at 6,144), under greedy decoding at temperature 0; the candidate arms change only the sampling: d1-qwen-sampling {"temperature": 0.6, "top_k": 20, "top_p": 0.95}; d2-qwen-sampling-presence {"presence_penalty": 1.5, "temperature": 0.6, "top_k": 20, "top_p": 0.95}; d3-temp-0.3 {"temperature": 0.3, "top_k": 20, "top_p": 0.95}; d4-greedy-presence {"presence_penalty": 1.5, "temperature": 0}
findings.remedy: none; the read reports the forced-close share (split by supplied-item bin), the empty-gold false-fill rows (split by forced status) and each arm's discordance against the lock beside the twin's.

findings.finding: The per-node thinking fields are composed at request time, keyed by the contact's ROLE ID, and a decoding arm's override is applied AFTER them and only to the four sampling keys, so a Solver decoding-arm contact carries the same budget 3072 / max_tokens 4096 / enable_thinking / seed as the delivering contact. Proven at the request level by tests/unit/test_decoding_variants_live.py and tests/unit/test_nxt_r4_registration.py and, for the cell, by the dry run (node_decoding and decoding_override per arm).

The twin aa (replicate_of lock) is the in-flight A/A: its request is the lock's in every declared field, so its SLU delta against lock is the offset o of the read and its discordance share the run-to-run baseline of a greedy request at 4 slots (the R2b analysis measured 25 % forced-status flips between two greedy arms). The 268-B cross-flight offsets (SLU +1.15, P3.1 -0.61) are reported beside, never used in a word.

The request seed (20260913) is the lock's for every arm. A sampling arm at that seed is reproducible only up to the serving geometry's batching nondeterminism, so the arms are single draws, not expectations: the read reports each sampling arm's discordance against the lock beside the twin's and never reads a single arm as a distribution.
findings.remedy: none; the discordance table is in the read.

findings.finding: temperature, top_p, top_k and presence_penalty are in core.model.request_types.ALLOWED_DECODING_KEYS and core.model.transport moves every decoding_params key it does not own to the top level of the OpenAI-compatible request body, which is where llama.cpp's server reads each of them (read from source, no server was contacted). The llama.cpp build commit is the one the runtime receipt records; a build that ignored a field would show as a zero discordance of that arm against the lock beside a non-zero one for the other arms.
findings.remedy: the smoke reads the four-row per-arm decode cost; the read reports discordance per arm.

findings.finding: Arm d4 keeps temperature 0 and adds presence_penalty 1.5. Whether the pinned llama.cpp sampler chain applies the penalty before the greedy pick is a property of that build (read it from the runtime receipt); a build that applies it makes d4 differ from the lock, a build that does not makes d4 a second spelling of the lock and its discordance equal to the twin's.
findings.remedy: none needed to fly: the read reports d4's discordance against the twin's, which shows which case held.
